c.tagline: Honduras's Caribbean party town and gateway to the Bay Islands and Pico Bonito.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are unmetered - agree the fare before getting in (short in-town hops are cheap, around 30-40 lempira). Colectivo taxis share fixed routes for a set fare. Uber coverage in La Ceiba is limited, so most rides are by street or hotel-arranged taxi.

emergency.note: 911 is the national emergency number connecting police, fire, and ambulance.

hood_desc: The downtown core around Parque Central and Avenida San Isidro, the city's main thoroughfare, lined with banks, markets, the cathedral and the Carnival parade route; the practical, walkable base for first-timers.

La Ceiba's famous nightlife and beach zone by the old pier, packed with bars, discos and seafood spots that give the city its title of 'Entertainment Capital of Honduras'; best for going out and beachfront energy.

The jungle-clad river gorge on the eastern edge of town at the gateway to Pico Bonito National Park, home to eco-lodges and Class III-IV whitewater rafting; the choice for rafting, hiking and nature over city life.

A modern residential and retail area about 2 km south of downtown, between the Megaplaza and Uniplaza malls; quieter and more spread out than the centre, and the part of town with the newer chain-style hotels.

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water only.

transit.pay: City buses and colectivo taxis take cash (lempiras) paid to the driver - a flat few-lempira fare. Regular taxis are unmetered, so agree the fare first. Uber has limited coverage.
transit.hours: Buses and colectivos run from early morning until around 7-8 PM; after dark, taxis are the way to get around.
transit.note: La Ceiba has no rail or metro (the old banana railway is long gone). Getting around is by city bus, colectivo and private taxi. The city is the Caribbean-coast gateway: ferries to the Bay Islands (Roatan and Utila) leave the Muelle de Cabotaje east of town, and the bus terminal west of the center runs long-distance coaches along the north coast.

landmarks: Pico Bonito National Park
A dramatic rainforest park rising behind the city, where jungle trails, waterfalls and toucans cloak the jagged 2,435-meter peak of Pico Bonito.
Río Cangrejal
Honduras's white-water capital, a boulder-strewn jungle river offering world-class rafting and riverside eco-lodges just minutes upstream from town.
Cuero y Salado Wildlife Refuge
A mangrove estuary reserve west of the city where boat safaris glide past manatees, howler monkeys and hundreds of bird species.
Catedral San Isidro and Parque Central
The city's twin-towered cathedral overlooking the palm-shaded central plaza, heart of La Ceiba's famous May carnival celebrations honoring its patron saint.
La Ceiba Malecón (seafront boardwalk)
The breezy Caribbean waterfront promenade near the old dock, lined with seafood stands and the best spot to watch fishermen and sunsets.
Museum of Butterflies and Other Insects
A surprising private collection of thousands of dazzling Honduran butterflies, moths and beetles, one of Central America's finest entomology displays.
Parque Swinford
A shady century-old park of towering trees and gazebos gifted by railroad-era banana companies, a green relic of La Ceiba's boom years.
Playa La Ensenada
A palm-fringed public beach east of the city where locals swim, eat fried fish and gaze across the water toward the Cayos Cochinos.
Reynaldo Canales Tourist Pier
A modern boardwalk pier extending into the Caribbean Sea, giving panoramic sunset views of the coastline and Pico Bonito mountain behind the city.
Paseo de los Ceibeños
A restored waterfront boardwalk built around La Ceiba's old pier, a quieter counterpart to the town's main Malecón for a stroll by the sea.

train.note: Honduras has no scheduled passenger railway. The national railway FNH cancelled its passenger trains in 2004, leaving only short freight lines around San Pedro Sula and Puerto Cortés and a few tourist and community remnants near La Ceiba, including the short line towards the Cuero y Salado wildlife refuge. There are no international rail links anywhere in Central America north of Panama, so travel to Guatemala, El Salvador or Nicaragua is by bus or air.

bus.note: No international coach starts in La Ceiba; you connect in San Pedro Sula, about 3-4 hours away by frequent buses costing around 100-200 lempiras. From San Pedro Sula, Tica Bus (https://ticabus.com/) runs to Guatemala, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama, and Hedman Alas operates comfortable services to Copán Ruinas, Guatemala City and Antigua. Buses in La Ceiba leave from the main terminal on the western edge of town, about 2 km from the centre; tickets are bought at the counter in cash and there is no online booking for most local operators. Travellers coming from Guatemala City normally allow 8-11 hours to San Pedro Sula before the onward leg.

ferry.note: La Ceiba is the mainland gateway to the Bay Islands and all sailings leave from the Muelle de Cabotaje, a short taxi ride east of the centre rather than from the town waterfront. The Galaxy Wave catamaran to Roatán runs twice daily each way, currently leaving La Ceiba around 09:30 and 16:30 and taking roughly 90 minutes, with Útila about an hour away and Guanaja served less often. Book online or through the operator's app in high season, and arrive an hour early for the security check. The crossing is notoriously choppy between December and February when northers blow - take seasickness tablets or fly with the local airlines instead.

half.name: Cayos Cochinos
half.blurb: A pristine archipelago of coral cays and Garifuna fishing villages in a marine reserve, reached by boat for snorkeling impossibly clear Caribbean water.

half.name: Sambo Creek
half.blurb: A lively Garifuna beach village east of town famous for coconut seafood soup, drumming culture and jungle hot springs in the hills behind.
